successors.name: United States of America
successors.text: the Haudenosaunee homeland in upstate New York, the Finger Lakes and the Mohawk valley, which the 1783 Treaty of Paris left to the United States ('no provisions were made for the Iroquois')

ledger.x: c. 1450: the Five Nations League of the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca is formed under the Great Law of Peace. 1638: the Wenro are dispersed.
1648: the Haudenosaunee strike the Wendat.
16 March 1649: the Haudenosaunee enter Wendake.
May 1649: the occupation ends in annexation (the gain below).
1649: Huronia falls.
1649: the Haudenosaunee take Huronia.
1650: the Petun are defeated and assimilated ('Petun (1650)').
1650: the Haudenosaunee attack the Neutral Nation ('1650-1651 attacks on the Neutrals').
1651: the Neutrals are gone.
1651: the Haudenosaunee take the Neutral country.
1654: the war on the Erie begins ('1654-1656 war against the Erie').
1656: the Erie confederacy is destroyed.
1656: the Haudenosaunee take the Erie shore of Lake Erie.
1659: the Ohio country passes to the Haudenosaunee on Cliopatria's shape.
1663: the Haudenosaunee besiege the Susquehannock.

c. 1670: the Ohio hunting grounds. 'Ohio River watershed became Haudenosaunee hunting grounds from about 1670'; the Nanfan page says the claim reached 'as far west as Quadoge (now Chicago)'. A claim, not settlement: the wars left it depopulated.
1670: the Mannahoac are driven from the northern Virginia Piedmont ('Mannahoac driven from the northern Virginia Piedmont').
1675: the Susquehannock war ends.
1675: the Susquehannock land passes to the Haudenosaunee.
1683: the claim reaches its largest, 570,382 km2.
1687: the claim thins at its edges.
1701: the hunting grounds are deeded to the English Crown.
1722: the Five Nations become the Six Nations ('They have also been called the Six Nations (Five Nations before 1722)').
1722: the Tuscarora join as the sixth nation.
1734: the Champlain shore leaves the shape.
1757: the heartland's northern and eastern edge thins.
1763: the rim of the Iroquois country passes to the British colonies on Cliopatria's shape.
1768: the Ohio hunting ground is ceded.
1769: the heartland shrinks to its core on Cliopatria's shape.
1779: the Sullivan Expedition marches into Iroquoia.
1779: the expedition ends on 3 October with about 40 Haudenosaunee villages razed and 'just over 5,000 Haudenosaunee' driven to Fort Niagara; it 'depopulated the area for post-war settlement'.
1784: the Six Nations cede their claims at Fort Stanwix.
1784: the Confederacy's territory passes under the United States.

wars.name: Mohawk-Mahican War
wars.outcome: The Mohawks defeated the Mahicans and secured direct access to Dutch trade at Fort Orange.

wars.name: Beaver Wars
wars.outcome: The Haudenosaunee destroyed the Wendat (1649), Petun (1650), Neutral (1651) and Erie (1656) and absorbed the Susquehannock (1675), claiming the Ohio country; French and Anishinaabe resistance from 1687 ended the conquests, and the Great Peace of Montreal (4…

wars.name: Sullivan Expedition
wars.outcome: About 40 Haudenosaunee villages razed and over 5,000 refugees driven to Fort Niagara; the area depopulated 'for post-war settlement'.

wars.name: Loyalist and Haudenosaunee raids on the Mohawk and Schoharie valleys
wars.outcome: Brant's raid on Harpersfield (April), the destruction of Caughnawaga (May) and Sir John Johnson's burning of 200 dwellings (October); no change of border.

certainty.note: Throughout the borders are approximate: the pages give peoples, hunting-ground claims and treaty lines in miles, not surveyed frontiers.
